title: History Reveals

body: Four of us visited Ridi Viharaya, an ancient temple situated in a small village “Ridigama” about 20 km from Kurunegala City, on 4th January 2017. One of the priests explained the historical significance of this temple. Around the 2nd century bc., a merchant carrying his wares when passing this area noticed a ripe jack fruit on a tree. He plucked it for his lunch. When he was readying for lunch he met a priest to whom he offered part of the jack fruit. After partaking this meal, the priest led him along to a cave and asked him to go in. Inside the cave was silver ore. The merchant collected a lump of this silver after hacking it with his axe and promptly took it away to his King Dutugamunu in Anuradhapura. The tale has it that the King excavated the silver for use in building the famed Ruwanweli stupa in Anuradhapura. The king Dutugamunu later built this temple at this location to display and demonstrate his gratitude. Coming down the steps on to the terrace one comes across an image house named ‘Waraka Walandu Viharaya’, the location where the priest is said to have partaken the ripe jack fruit. The building has a stone roof supported by eight stone pillars. Inside is a seated Buddha statue.Passing this image house and the Bodhi tree we came over to ‘hevisi mandapaya’ (drummer’s pavilion) that is under renovation. When we visited that morning the main temple was closed. We waited in the courtyard between the drummer’s pavilion and the main temple until it was opened. We chatted with the ladies and gentlemen from the Department of Archaeology and post-graduate students from Kelaniya University who were engaged in restoration work. Some of them gave us more information about the temple and its surrounds. The courtyard is also home to some pieces of sculpture. The Maha Viharaya – The main temple – is housed under a large cave in a massive rock outcrop. This is said to be located where the silver ore was found. No photographs with flash were allowed within although there was no objection to capturing a few photos with my cell phone. Inside the Mahavihara is a 30 foot reclining Buddha statue. The gold plated statue in a glass casing is said to be the original donated by King Dutugamunu. The main temple had been patronised by kings such as Parakramabahu the great (2nd century ad) and later renovated by King Kirthi Sri Rajasinghe during the 18th century. During the renovation of the temple in the 18th century, the Dutch governer of then Ceylon, had donated some Dutch tiles. These had been haphazardly arranged below the reclining Buddha statue, some bottom to top, some sideways, showing that the tiler had been oblivious to the significance of the stories of Jesus represented in the tiles. Uda Vihara or upper temple access is through a side door of the main temple. In addition to the main chamber that houses the Buddha statue, the other two chambers in the upper temple have statues of deity and some curious drawings.Long flight of stone steps lead you to the stupa. A byway along this path leads to some caves. There are steps cut into the rock quite close to the enclosure containing the stupa. There is also a little pond to one side of the stupa that probably had been used by devotees to wash flowers offered.The visit to Ridi Viharaya took us about 2 hours. There is no entry fee. On the way back we stopped at Ridigama and had a hearty breakfast of local cuisine at a very clean little cooperative restaurant run by a group of ladies. All in all a fruitful, productive, rewarding and an enjoyable morning.
title: Silver Temple with a Historic Past

body: This creation belongs to the second century, the Polonnaruwa kingdom era. This was my first visit to this archaeological site. The roof is stone made flat structure using stone blocks. According to the archaeology experts, the most venerable monks occupied such places and the design reflects it by living with the nature without damaging it. University students and staff were working hard under the guidance of the Archaeology department to preserve the drawings on the stone.

body: Bit out of the main road but still within reach when travelling towards the ancient cities of Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya or Dambulla, this cave temple on hilly terrain is worth the visit. Series of ancient statues of Lord Buddha in seated, standing and reclining posture are set inside several image houses built within the cave. Temple complex is spread out over several terraces. Before the main cave temple is a smaller Kandyan era shrine built against a rock. It has carved stone pillars supporting a stone roof and a small chamber with a seated Buddha statue. Hundreds of wall murals decorate the shrines.

title: Ridi Viharaya (Silver Temple)
body: Situated just within 8 kms from Kurunegala on Keppitigala road, this is one of the oldest temples in Sri Lanka which was built by King Dutugamunu who unified the island under his control. Temple was built in gratitude, according to legend a group of traders travelling to hill country wanted to rest their cattles (bullock carts pulled by bulls) went in search of fruits, found a riped jack fruit. They wanted to offer a portion to meditating arahaths (monks). After accepting the jack fruit, one arahaths show them a way to an area where they found this silver ore. Traders took a sample to king and he used the silver to pay his workmen who were building the King's masterpiece Ruwanweliseya Dagaba in Anuradhapura.You can see the glass encased Gold plated Buddha statue and old paintings together with ivory and crafted gem inserted doors which supplied sun light to the inner temple.
